dse_runs.notes: NCO/DDS sin-cos for DUC: need 1 sample/clock at >=250 MSPS, max_abs_err <= 2^-13. Minimise LUTs (HV ref 4000), maximise accuracy_bits (HV ref 13); select min luts. Memory is off, so no prior lessons: explore broadly across iterative / unrolled_k / pipelined / pipelined_m families, and make sure the front is well spread on the LUT-vs-accuracy trade-off. Prefer designs that keep throughput >= 250 MSPS with margin (pipelined/unrolled with enough parallelism) and error comfortably under 2^-13.

l3: not verified in this campaign: no recorded L3 row; a fresh exhaustive run (W=18) is too heavy for a live campaign
l4: no recorded synthesis for this design (L4 is not run live in campaigns)
final_text: Campaign complete — the queue held a single spec, `dds_250msps` (NCO/DDS sin-cos for a digital up-converter: throughput ≥ 250 MSPS, max_abs_err ≤ 2^-13, objectives min LUTs / max accuracy_bits, select min LUTs). Memory was switched off, so `recall` returned nothing and `remember` stored nothing. I spent the spec's entire L1 budget in one `run_dse` call (400/400 evaluations, 0 left; inner graph ran map_front → refine → map_front → stop), which yielded a 30-design feasible, non-dominated front — all pipelined-family designs, with the LUT/accuracy trade-off driven by `n_iter` (~65 LUTs per extra iteration at W=18) and by `data_width=19 + frac_guard=1 + trunc` as the cheaper route past 14 accuracy bits. The spec has no system scenario, so there were no `sys_*` bounds to simulate and `simulate_system` was unnecessary; the graph's internal L2 shortlist covered that rung. The `ladder` sub-agent then ran L3/L4/L5: `verify_rtl` produced no row (a live exhaustive W=18 run was declined as too heavy; only generator-level verification over 47 configs exists), `synthesize` had no recorded synthesis for this design, and `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data` — which is not a WINNER CHANGE, so `reexplore` was correctly not invoked. I finalized the min-LUTs selection: `pipelined:data_width=18,n_iter=15,angle_guard=2,frac_guard=0,rounding=round` with luts=920 (estimate), accuracy_bits=13.2, ffs=953, throughput_msps=264 (estimate), max_abs_err=0.000109 = 2^-13.17 (exact, golden model) — feasible on both constraints, though with thin margins (~11% under the error limit, ~5.6% over the throughput requirement); the recorded fallback if measurements later contradict it is `n_iter=16` (luts=985, err=8.35e-05). All numbers above carry their provenance: LUTs/FFs/throughput are cost-model estimates, the error is exact, and nothing is measured.
